text:
Why does a computer need examples in order to learn to recognize earthquakes?

A computer can’t simply "find earthquakes." Humans need to decide what data to provide, identify examples, determine what patterns matter. Let’s look at seismic data from stations around Anchorage. Can you find earthquakes in the data?

Instructions

1) In the WaveRunner on the right, click on the box that says “Choose a station.” Scroll through the list and choose one seismograph station.

2) Click on the box that says “Choose a model” and click on “compact model.”

3) Type in a date range (anytime between January 1, 2018 to the present day).

4) In the bottom control bar of the WaveRunner, click the "Timeline It!" button (the button furthest to the right). The Timeline will display the data for the station and dates you selected right below the WaveRunner.

5) Use the Timeline to search through the seismic data for signals of earthquakes. Be sure to check that each signal you choose matches the shape of the earthquake signal above!

6) When you have found a signal, record its station, date, and start time in the table.
